Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

In 'до встречи' = until we meet. Common feminine noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Synonym of едва. Core Russian adv meaning 'barely, hardly' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Он так устал, что еле шёл домой.
examples.trans: He was so tired that he could barely walk home.

examples.text: Аркашка, ты еле стираешь! Сильнее три!
examples.trans: Arkashka, you're barely washing! Rub harder!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to live'.

examples.trans: I live in a communal flat.

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: Asks about the purpose. Core Russian adv meaning 'what for, why' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Agreeing, often reluctantly. Core Russian part meaning 'all right, OK' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: + infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice

examples.trans: Arkasha, I didn't expect that. Thank you!

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'cool' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.trans: This is a very cool movie.

examples.text: У тебя сегодня очень прикольная причёска.
examples.trans: You have a really cool hairstyle today.

присесть.gloss: to sit down (for a moment), to take a seat

meanings.en: to sit down, to have a seat
meanings.note: Polite invitation: Присядьте!. Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'сесть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sit down (for a moment), to take a seat', paired with 'присаживаться'.

examples.trans: He sat down on the chair.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, присядьте. Попробуйте чай с сушками, очень вкусные.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, have a seat. Try the tea with bread rings, they're very tasty.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?
